# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Full working reference: epam/dmtools-dart .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml
      - run: echo "Adapt runner steps from the machine-kit reference (see header comment)"

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1031
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1031
- **Title**: gh-1029 AI Teammate self-retriggers on its own lifecycle labels (labeled event starts a no-op run every status:* write)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1029` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +111
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T08:47:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T08:57:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1029
### What changed
Gated the AI Teammate `labeled` trigger at job level: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` now proceeds only when the added label is an arming label (`agent:dev`, `agent:develop`, `agent:review`, `agent:rework`, `pr_approved`) — lifecycle labels (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …) skip the job and never allocate a runner. Same gate added to the `guard` job in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`.

### Key decisions
- `on:` cannot filter by label name, so the gate lives in the job `if:` keyed on `github.event.action` — the old assignee-only clause admitted *any* labeled event on an assigned issue (the gh-1029 self-retrigger: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027)
- Kept prior semantics: `assigned` still requires the `ai-teammate` assignee; `pr_approved` stays in the arming set; `workflow_dispatch` (SM reconciler path) untouched
- Template fixed too — its `guard` job previously allocated a runner on every label write just to decide `run=false`
- New gh-1029 contract suite in `test_workflowLint.js` pins the arming-label set, action-keyed branches, and dispatch path for both files

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_workflowLint.json   # 30 passed
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # 3859 passed, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Gate flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  E[issues event] --> A{action}
  A -->|assigned| B[assignee == ai-teammate?]
  A -->|labeled| C{label in arming set?}
  A -->|other| X[skip — no runner]
  B -->|yes| R[teammate leg runs]
  B -->|no| X
  C -->|yes| R
  C -->|no: status:*, ai_developed, ...| X
  D[workflow_dispatch] --> R
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit
{"path":"workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template"}

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then

          fi

Gated the AI Teammate `labeled` trigger at job level: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` now proceeds only when the added label is an arming label (`agent:dev`, `agent:develop`, `agent:review`, `agent:rework`, `pr_approved`) — lifecycle labels (`status:*`, `ai_developed`, …) skip the job and never allocate a runner. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.

# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Fu…

Now let me look at where labels get added and how arming labels are consumed, to validate the new gate. Key questions:

1. `pr_approved` — in old stub gate, `labeled && label.name == 'pr_approved'` triggered regardless of assignee. New gate keeps that. OK.
2. `agent:rework`, `agent:review`, `agent:dev`, `agent:develop` — new arming labels. Who adds them and how does the workflow get triggered? If SM adds `agent:review` label with a PAT, the labeled event fires → gate admits. Good.
3. Concern: the stub's `labeled` path previously admitted any label on an assigned issue — was that intentional for other labels? E.g., does anything rely on "issue assigned to ai-teammate + some label write → re-run dev leg"? E.g., a human removes and re-adds a label to retrigger? The old behavior: any labeled event on assigned issue triggered the factory with leg=' (empty). The factory guard derives the leg. If an issue is assigned to ai-teammate and someone adds e.g. `bug` label, the old workflow would run (guard decides dev/bug runner). New gate blocks that. But that's fine per gh-1029 intent; `assigned` event fires on assign.

4. Template guard: old gate had no job-level if — guard ran on every event. The new guard drops the assignee check for `assigned` events: `(github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.action == 'assigned')` — any assigned event enters the guard, and the shell script decides run=false if assignee isn't ai-teammate. That preserves guard-script semantics (script checks ASSIGNES). Fine — guard shell still decides.

5. But wait: template's guard for `labeled` admits arming labels. What about a labeled event with e.g. `agent:skip` added to an assigned issue — old behavior: guard runs → script sees agent:skip → run=false. New: job skipped entirely. Equivalent outcome, less runner. Good.

6. Potential issue: in the template's guard, the `if:` skips the job — but the `teammate` job has `needs: guard` and `if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'`. If guard is skipped, needs.guard.outputs is empty → 'true' != → teammate skipped. OK.

7. Security/CI safety: workflow files changed — check permissions: stub already has permissions block; template has permissions. No new secrets. The gate uses github.event context safely.

8. Test file: check the new test code style — GralJS constraints (no let/const/arrow functions). New test code uses `var` and function expressions. Good. But is test_workflowLint.js a "packed" runtime file? No, it's a unit test run in dmtools GralJS. Uses `file_read` global. Check how STUB and TEMPLATE are defined in the test file — need to read the rest of the file to see STUB/TEMPLATE loading.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. The old assignee-only clause
    # admitted any labeled event on an assigned issue, so each leg
    # re-triggered a guaranteed no-op run that parked in the same
    # concurrency group (live: run 39111715487 → 39111765329 on #1027,
    # 2026-10-18). The gate therefore keys the action: `assigned` requires
    # the ai-teammate assignee; `labeled` proceeds ONLY for the arming
    # labels — lifecycle labels never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
      # 2026-10-17 incident: GitHub's ubuntu-slim SKU started force-cancelling
      # teammate jobs at exactly ~15m24s (6/6 legs tonight, 15:20–15:26;
      # "The operation was canceled" from the control plane, conclusion=cancelled).
      # Yesterday the same SKU ran legs for 24 min fine. dmtools-dart legs on
      # ubuntu-24.04 are unaffected. Owner decision: CI checks stay on slim,
      # ai-teammate legs move to ubuntu-latest until slim is healthy again.
      runner: 'ubuntu-latest'
    secrets: inherit
{"path":"workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template"}

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60

      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic
